elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Retained 7.5(a): "On its resignation or termination, the Servicer will cooperate with the Issuer, the Owner Trustee, the Indenture Trustee and the Successor Servicer in effecting ... an orderly transition of such rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer." The added assistance period and the amended 7.5(b) deadline both run from "the effective date of its resignation or termination," so every covered cessation event (resignation or termination of the Servicer role, including on wind-up of the Agreement) carries the transition obligation. There is no separate "expiry" concept for the Servicer appointment in this structure, so the condition does not create a gap.

elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance for up to six months.
elements.evidence: The inserted language commits only to "such transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days after the effective date of its resignation or termination" — no six-month period is offered anywhere in 7.5.

elements.element: Transition assistance is charged at then-current rates.
elements.evidence: No rate mechanic appears in the rendered 7.5(a)/(b); 7.5(c) instead allocates transition expenses to the terminated Servicer (more favourable to us, but it is not a then-current-rates term as the preferred element states).

elements.element: Vendor returns Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Amended 7.5(b): "Within thirty (30) days after the effective date of its resignation or termination, the predecessor Servicer will ... (ii) deliver to the Successor Servicer the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer." The open-ended "as soon as practicable" trigger has been replaced by a fixed outside date.

elements.element: Customer Data is returned in a standard machine-readable format.
elements.evidence: 7.5(b) specifies no format for the Receivable Files or the accounts and records; no machine-readable or commonly used format wording was inserted.

elements.element: Vendor certifies deletion of Customer Data after its return.
elements.evidence: No deletion obligation and no written certification of deletion appears anywhere in the rendered 7.5.

elements.element: Transition obligations apply on expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Same retained trigger in 7.5(a) ("On its resignation or termination ... an orderly transition of such rights and obligations to the Successor Servicer"), and both operative edits are anchored to "the effective date of its resignation or termination," so the assistance and delivery duties attach to each covered cessation event rather than to an anticipated one only.

elements.element: Vendor provides at least 90 days of transition assistance.
elements.evidence: Inserted in 7.5(a): "and will provide such transition assistance for at least ninety (90) days after the effective date of its resignation or termination." "Such transition assistance" refers back to the cooperation/orderly-transition duty in the same sentence, so the floor is tied to a defined obligation rather than an undefined trigger.

elements.element: Vendor exports Customer Data within 30 days after expiry or termination.
elements.evidence: Amended 7.5(b) imposes a hard 30-day deadline for transfer of funds and delivery of "the Receivable Files and the accounts and records maintained by the Servicer" to the Successor Servicer, replacing "As soon as practicable." Delivery to the Successor Servicer is the structural equivalent of return to the Issuer here. The retained second sentence excusing items "restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies" is a pre-existing scope limitation aimed at Servicer processes and third-party-restricted materials, not a timing defeasance of the express Receivable Files/records obligation.

reasons: Fallback is position-complete: the trigger element was already met by retained 7.5(a), operation 1 supplies the 90-day assistance floor, and operation 2 converts "as soon as practicable" into a fixed 30-day delivery deadline.
Preferred is not complete and is correctly not claimed: no six-month period, no then-current-rates term, no machine-readable format, and no certified deletion after return.

Minimality holds. Only two edits were made, each traceable to a fallback element; "at least ninety (90) days" sits exactly at the threshold without exceeding it, and replacing "As soon as practicable" is necessary because retaining it alongside a 30-day outside date would create competing timing standards. No survival tail, expense language, format, deletion or certification extras were bolted on.

Intent preserved: the 7.5(b) carve-out for processes, models and servicing software, the funds-transfer limb, and the 7.5(c) expense allocation all survive unchanged; no defined term is orphaned and no cross-reference dangles.

Residual risk to note for the drafter (not a fallback failure, and not a defect the fallback checklist requires curing): the retained sentence excusing delivery of "anything covered by a restriction on transfer or assignment or a confidentiality agreement or otherwise restricted by legal, regulatory, privacy or data protection policies" is broad enough to be argued against Receivable Files containing obligor data. If the team wants belt-and-braces, the minimal cure is a carve-back such as "except that this sentence does not limit clause (ii) above," but adding it now would be an extra beyond the selected checklist.

If the preferred position is later pursued, the exact repairs are: extend 7.5(a) assistance to six months at the Servicer's then-current rates, specify a commonly used machine-readable format in 7.5(b)(ii), and add a post-delivery deletion-and-written-certification limb.
